title: Market Pattern Learning Library
description: 35 candlestick patterns and 18 chart-pattern topics, with original English teaching text and synthetic drawings.
notice: For education only. Patterns can fail. No success rates are claimed. Examples are synthetic and are not personalized investment advice.
rightsNote: Fresh wording, organization, code and synthetic drawings. No PDF pages, screenshots, logos or copied paragraphs are included. This is not legal clearance or a guarantee against copyright claims.

lessons.title: Read one candle
lessons.body: A candle summarizes one interval using open, high, low and close. The body connects open and close; wicks reach the high and low. An up candle closes above its own open, not necessarily above the previous close.
points: Body = abs(close - open). Range = high - low.
Upper wick = high - max(open, close). Lower wick = min(open, close) - low.
A small body means limited net movement, not necessarily low volume.
Color schemes vary; use open and close values to determine direction.

lessons.title: Locate the pattern
lessons.body: A pattern describes behavior rather than proving what comes next. Read the prior trend and surrounding price levels before assigning meaning.
points: Support and resistance are areas of previous reactions; both can fail.
Compare candle dimensions with recent volatility.
Keep higher-timeframe context and nearby obstacles visible.
Do not infer participant identity, intent or manipulation from a shape.

lessons.title: Separate candidates from confirmation
lessons.body: A candidate has the expected geometry. A confirmed example also satisfies a rule chosen beforehand, such as a completed close outside a boundary. Confirmation cannot eliminate false signals.
points: Wait for the bar to finish before classifying its final shape.
A wick beyond a level differs from a close beyond it.
Retests are optional and may never occur.
Historical labels must not depend on future information unavailable at signal time.

lessons.title: Plan hypothetical risk
lessons.body: An invalidation level marks where a scenario loses its basis. A stop order is an execution tool and can fill beyond the intended level during gaps or poor liquidity.
points: For simple cash equities: units = floor(cash risk budget / abs(entry - stop)).
Example only: a 500-unit cash risk budget and 5-unit price distance imply 100 shares before costs. This is arithmetic, not an allocation recommendation.
Planned reward-to-risk = abs(target - entry) / abs(entry - stop). Reject zero distance and targets on the wrong side.
Include spread, fees, slippage and gap risk. Contracts and leveraged products need multipliers and additional analysis.
A candidate can be skipped when nearby opposing structure leaves too little room.

lessons.title: Evaluate evidence
lessons.body: This library supplies no win rates and implements no trading strategy. A recognizable historical shape is not proof of positive returns.
points: Define market, timeframe, entries, exits and costs before testing.
Include failures and ambiguous examples.
Keep development data separate from evaluation data.
Report sample size, expectancy and drawdown alongside any win rate.
Volume can add context where meaningful; it is not a universal guarantee.

lessons.title: Check the market data
lessons.body: Candles and gaps depend on session settings, liquidity and data quality. Missing records or inconsistent corporate-action adjustments can create misleading formations.
points: Use one instrument, timezone, session definition and adjustment policy per series.
Reject non-finite values and records where high < max(open, close) or low > min(open, close).
Handle zero-range candles before calculating ratios.
All diagrams here use invented values and are not historical evidence.

lessons.title: Before building automated detection
lessons.body: The supplied module is an educational content library, not an automatic detector. A production scanner needs precise definitions, appropriate data and independent evaluation.
points: Parameterize body size, wick ratios, trend lookback, gaps and near-equality tolerances.
Common ratios such as 2:1 are heuristics rather than universal thresholds.
Distinguish candidate, confirmed and invalidated states.
Do not add unsupported accuracy percentages or confidence scores.

patterns.name: Ascending Channel
patterns.context: During higher highs and higher lows.
patterns.overview: The structure describes an upward trend.
patterns.confirmation: Lower-boundary break warns of weakness; upper-boundary break may indicate acceleration.
patterns.invalidation: For a bearish break thesis, recovery into channel and new highs weaken it.
cautions: The channel is not inherently bearish; a downside break can lead to consolidation.
patterns.targetMethod: The shape supplies no reliable fixed target. In a hypothetical study, compare nearby opposing support or resistance with the planned risk distance.
patterns.timeframeNote: Use completed candles from one consistent timeframe. Session boundaries, liquidity, costs and noise affect interpretation.

patterns.name: Broadening Formation
patterns.context: In a volatile range or near a possible transition.
recognition: common megaphone has higher highs and lower lows.
tilted variants may rise or fall.
patterns.overview: The distribution of traded prices widens rather than compresses.
patterns.confirmation: Boundary break with follow-through; direction is unresolved beforehand.
patterns.invalidation: Rapid return inside the expanding range.
cautions: Large swings create wide risk distances and do not prove manipulation.
variants: Ascending broadening structures have two rising, diverging boundaries. Descending broadening structures have two falling, diverging boundaries. The horizontal megaphone expands in both directions.
patterns.targetMethod: The shape supplies no reliable fixed target. In a hypothetical study, compare nearby opposing support or resistance with the planned risk distance.

patterns.name: Bump and Run

recognition: steeper bump away from lead-in boundary.

patterns.overview: An accelerated move loses support from its earlier trend structure.
patterns.confirmation: Top: close below lead-in support. Mirrored bottom: above lead-in resistance.
patterns.invalidation: Failed trendline break followed by renewed movement toward the extreme.
cautions: Angles depend on screen scale; the pattern does not reveal deceptive intent.

patterns.name: Cup and Handle
patterns.context: Usually a rounded consolidation in an uptrend; inverse version is bearish.
recognition: Rounded cup instead of one sharp V.
patterns.overview: A longer recovery and a smaller pause precede an attempted breakout.
patterns.confirmation: Regular: close above handle and rim. Inverse: close below corresponding support.
patterns.invalidation: Regular: loss of handle low. Inverse: break above handle high.
cautions: A deep or prolonged handle can indicate a different structure.
patterns.targetMethod: Cup depth can be projected from the rim breakout. Consider handle failure and nearer price obstacles before the projection.

patterns.name: Head and Shoulders
patterns.context: Regular version after an advance; inverse after a decline.
recognition: Regular: middle peak higher than shoulders.
inverse: middle trough lower than shoulders.
patterns.overview: A failed extension of the prior trend creates a possible turning structure.
patterns.confirmation: Regular: close below neckline. Inverse: close above neckline.
patterns.invalidation: Failed neckline break; movement beyond right shoulder is a common structural reference.
cautions: Shoulders can differ and necklines can slope. A break is not certainty.
patterns.targetMethod: Measure vertically from head to neckline at the head, then project from the breakout in its direction. Mirror the construction for an inverse formation.

patterns.confirmation: Later break below second low.
patterns.invalidation: Recovery deep into the first body weakens the shallow-rebound premise.
cautions: Use the prior low as reference, not the prior close. This is conventionally a bearish continuation candidate.

patterns.name: Pennant
patterns.context: After a strong directional impulse.
recognition: compact pause with lower highs and higher lows.
patterns.overview: A short contraction interrupts the previous impulse.
patterns.confirmation: Close outside in prior impulse direction; opposite break requires reassessment.
patterns.invalidation: Re-entry followed by movement through the opposite boundary.
cautions: No fixed five-wave count is required. Without a pole, consider a triangle instead.
patterns.targetMethod: The pole length is sometimes projected from the breakout. An extended impulse can make this idealized projection unrealistic.

patterns.name: Wedge
patterns.context: Within a trend or near a turning area.
recognition: Both boundaries slope in the same direction and converge.
rising version has higher highs and lows.
falling version has lower highs and lows.
patterns.overview: Progress continues but the available range narrows.
patterns.confirmation: Rising wedge: close below lower boundary. Falling wedge: close above upper boundary.
patterns.invalidation: Failed break back inside; opposite-boundary break further contradicts scenario.
cautions: Wedges may reverse or continue trends. Parallel channels are a different structure.
